text:
Naomi Feldman: hey folks, starting security review thread for Shadow Traffic evals. main Q: for LLM-as-judge we’re talking about storing prompts + outputs (primary + shadow) so we can run scoring + later audits. what exactly are we persisting and what’s the default retention?

Dylan Brooks: thx Naomi. current proposal from product: persist sampled payloads for judge + “debug samples” in Console (so customers can click into a few examples). default retention we had penciled was 14d for beta.

Marcus Lin: 14d with raw prompts/outputs is going to be a hard sell unless it’s opt-in + tightly restricted. can we split: (1) derived metrics tables (scores, latency, token counts) vs (2) raw content samples stored separately?

Logan Wright: yes. telemetry pipeline already separates event metrics from “payload blobs”. event record in warehouse would have request_id, route_id, shadow_target_id, aggregate counters, judge outputs (structured), but no raw prompt/response. raw would go to restricted blob storage keyed by request_id.

Naomi Feldman: +1. we need clear data classification + access controls for the blob store path. who can read it? how is it audited?

Kevin Osei: proposal: payload blobs live under Restricted Logging boundary (same pattern as incident debug logs). access via oncall-approved group + JIT (time-bound) grants. all reads logged to audit sink. no “browsing” from Console unless customer explicitly enables “payload samples” and we can enforce tenant scoping.

Olivia Grant: judge scoring needs the content at scoring time. but we don’t need to persist it long-term to compute aggregate metrics. could we do “in-flight scoring” (shadow runner calls judge immediately) and only store (a) scores, (b) small, redacted sample set when configured?

Marcus Lin: that’s the right default. store derived signals by default; content storage optional.

Dylan Brooks: question: PM wants customers to be able to debug why a judge score dropped (like format adherence failing). if we don’t store any samples, it’s hard.

Naomi Feldman: I’m ok with samples, but needs: (1) explicit tenant opt-in, (2) default off, (3) minimal retention, (4) redaction, and (5) restricted access.

Allison Grant: also reminder: metric tags must not include free-form fields (prompt, user_id, tool args). we saw early drafts that included `customer_prompt_template_id` and some `tool_name` strings; those are ok if allowlisted + bounded cardinality.

Logan Wright: yup. for shadow_eval metrics we’re allowlisting tags + bucketing. no raw.

Nadia Rahman: on cost/metering side: we’ll attribute judge tokens + shadow tokens, but billing records also must not include prompt/output. just counts.

Naomi Feldman: can someone write down the proposed retention defaults? we need something crisp for SOC2 story.

Kevin Osei: draft defaults:
- Derived metrics (warehouse tables / time-series): 30d standard (matches other Console metrics), configurable higher for enterprise.
- Payload blobs (prompts/outputs): default OFF. if enabled, default retention 7d, configurable down to 24h, up to 14d w/ Security approval.
- Judge “explanations” (the judge model’s rationale text): treat as output content → same as payload blob policy (off by default, or store only normalized rubric fields).

Sana Farid: +1 on not storing judge rationale by default. we can store structured scores + a small enum-ish “failure_reason” field (e.g., `invalid_json`, `missing_field`, `refusal`, `safety_flag`) so we can debug without raw text.

Olivia Grant: we can adjust judge prompt to output JSON only (no prose), so the “explanation” is bounded. still could include user content if judge echoes though. need to instruct judge to never quote the input.

Marcus Lin: even with instructions, models can echo. safer to: (a) discard judge free-text, (b) log only parsed fields, (c) if parsing fails, log error type not raw completion.

Dylan Brooks: ok. but for beta customers asking for “examples”, can we store a handful of samples per day per route?

Kevin Osei: yes, with quotas. like “max 50 samples/day/route” and hard cap by tenant. also store only redacted versions (PII filters) and truncate to N chars to reduce leakage.

Naomi Feldman: redaction specifics?

Olivia Grant: PR in progress adds PII filters (emails, phone, SSN-ish, credit cards) + configurable regex allow/deny lists. default mode: redact before writing blob.

Marcus Lin: we also need a policy story for “customer data residency”. if a EU customer enables samples, the blob must stay in EU region and not replicate to US for analytics.

Logan Wright: we can keep blobs in regional object store (same region as request processing) and only write derived metrics cross-region if allowed by tenant config. for strict residency tenants, derived metrics also stay regional (we already have per-region datasets).

Talia Benson: pulling this into the beta checklist. do we have customer-facing copy for “shadow eval payload storage is optional”? Marissa asked.

Naomi Feldman: we’ll give PM language, but only after we lock the defaults.

Dylan Brooks: current plan was “Shadow Evals stores evaluation samples to help you debug regressions.” sounds like we need to change to “optional”.

Allison Grant: and we should be explicit that shadowing does not impact the primary response path, but does generate additional processing (and potentially logs) depending on config.

Naomi Feldman: access controls: can Console users see samples?

Kevin Osei: only if tenant enables `shadow_payload_samples` AND user has a specific role (e.g., `EvalDebugViewer`). otherwise Console shows aggregate charts only. any sample view should be behind an extra click-through (warning banner) + audit record.

Marcus Lin: and support/Redwood staff access should be break-glass only. no standing access.

Logan Wright: we can implement “customer-managed support bundle” style: customer generates a time-bound support token to let us view samples for X hours.

Naomi Feldman: good. also need to clarify what we store for “primary” vs “shadow”: are we storing both completions?

Olivia Grant: scoring needs both to compare. but we can store only shadow completion + a reference to primary (or vice versa). for sample debugging, it’s most useful to see both. so: if samples enabled → store both redacted. if not enabled → store neither, only the computed comparison signals.

Sana Farid: computed signals we need for gating: win-rate, tie-rate, format_valid_rate delta, safety outcome delta, latency/cost deltas. none requires raw text at rest.

Dylan Brooks: ok. what about “replay” later with a new judge prompt? some folks asked.

Marcus Lin: that’s a non-goal unless customer explicitly opts into longer retention + we have a clear legal/compliance basis. don’t bake that into beta.

Naomi Feldman: agreed. ship with “no replay by default”.

Kevin Osei: action items:
1) I’ll draft Restricted Logging / RBAC + JIT access doc for shadow payload samples.
2) @Olivia Grant update judge output format to minimize echo + ensure we only store parsed rubric fields.
3) @Dylan Brooks update product copy + Console spec: payload samples are opt-in + retention default 7d.
4) @Logan Wright confirm regional storage wiring + ensure warehouse tables exclude raw.

Dylan Brooks: :thumbsup: will update spec + ping Marissa.

Olivia Grant: ack, will adjust judge prompt + parser behavior.

Logan Wright: ack. will also add a lint check to reject any telemetry fields named `prompt`, `input_text`, `completion_text` etc.

Naomi Feldman: thanks all. I’ll summarize for the security sign-off: derived metrics ok; payload samples opt-in, redacted, regional, short retention, restricted access + audited. if anything changes from this, loop us in before beta enablement.
